chunks: And as for what Muhammad ibn Qays narrated via the first chain from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Imam Ali (peace be upon him) ruled regarding a female slave whom the son of her master sold while his father was absent, and a man bought her, and she bore a boy from him. Then the first master arrived and disputed with the second master, saying: 'This is my female slave; my son sold her without my permission.' He said: 'Take your female slave and her son.' The buyer entreated him, saying: 'Take his son,' meaning the son of the one who sold you the female slave, until he pays you what he sold you for. When the seller took the son, the father said: 'Send back my son.' He said: 'By Allah, I will not send back your son until you send back my son.' When the first master of the female slave saw this, he approved the sale of his son. The meaning of this report is that he ordered him to hold onto the seller's son because the debt is attached to the son, and it is obligatory upon him to compensate the owner of the girl with the price of the son, and to free the buyer's son from him and return him to him. When he did that, the father approved the sale of his son, so the children became free. And he did not do that because it is valid for him to enslave his free children for the sake of his son, and the meaning in it is what we have said.
ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling when a master's son sells a female slave without permission and she bears a child?
ai.summary: In this case from *al-Istibsar*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) resolved a dispute over a female slave sold by her minor owner's son, ruling that the buyer could retain the son as collateral until the purchase price was settled. This decision highlights the Shia legal principle of *ilhaq* (attachment), where the child's status follows the free parent, and demonstrates how the father's subsequent ratification of the sale led to the son's manumission, illustrating the interplay between debt attachment and freedom in inheritance and property law.
